title: ttnn.ge / ttnn.le (tensor-scalar): ge/le are lane-wise complements of lt/gt, so they cannot match IEEE NaN semantics, and heaviside cannot emit NaN at all - the tensor-tensor kernels (2026) already carry the explicit NaN rejection
body:
**Component / Area:** kernels

The tensor-scalar comparison kernels still carry their original 2023 form. The tensor-tensor comparison kernels were rewritten in 2026 with explicit NaN rejection that the scalar kernels never received. The same public op therefore runs two different kernels depending on the overload, and only one of them can be NaN-correct:

- The scalar overload `ge(Tensor, float)` reaches `calculate_unary_ge` (`ckernel_sfpu_unary_comp.h`, 2023) via `ttnn::ge_unary` and `unary_ge_tile`: [`binary.cpp:491`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/main/ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/eltwise/binary/binary.cpp#L491), [`unary.cpp:274`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/main/ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/eltwise/unary/unary.cpp#L274), [`comp.h:198-200`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/main/tt_metal/hw/inc/api/compute/eltwise_unary/comp.h#L198-L200)
- The tensor overload `ge(Tensor, Tensor)` reaches `calculate_binary_comp_fp32_weak_ordered` (`ckernel_sfpu_binary_comp.h`, 2026) through binary_ng

The scalar comparison kernels are byte-identical on Wormhole and Blackhole, and heaviside's branch logic is identical on both.

### The core defect needs no hardware to prove

`calculate_unary_ge` and `calculate_unary_lt` evaluate the same predicate and return opposite constants ([`ckernel_sfpu_unary_comp.h:99-134`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/main/tt_metal/hw/ckernels/wormhole_b0/metal/llk_api/llk_sfpu/ckernel_sfpu_unary_comp.h#L99-L134)):

```c
// lt:                          // ge:
v_if(v < s) { v = 1.0f; }       v_if(v < s) { v = 0.0f; }
v_else      { v = 0.0f; }       v_else      { v = 1.0f; }
```

So `ge(x, s) == 1.0 - lt(x, s)` holds on every lane by construction, and likewise `le(x, s) == 1.0 - gt(x, s)`. The reference (IEEE 754, torch) requires every ordered comparison with NaN to be false: `torch.lt`, `le`, `gt`, `ge` all return False on NaN; only `ne` returns True. Two ops defined as complements of each other cannot both return 0.0 on a NaN lane. Whatever truth value the SFPU assigns to `NaN < s`, exactly one member of each pair diverges from torch. That claim is independent of the hardware's compare behavior.

### Expected direction, stated as contingent

Two artifacts in the tree indicate the SFPU float predicate cannot see NaN: #52036 (the xlogy guard `in1 == nan` can never be true), and [`ckernel_sfpu_comp.h:108-150`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/main/tt_metal/hw/ckernels/wormhole_b0/metal/llk_api/llk_sfpu/ckernel_sfpu_comp.h#L108-L150), where the `*z` comparison kernels detect NaN with integer `|v| > inf` chains precisely because the float predicate does not. Under that behavior (`NaN < s` evaluates false), the expected outputs for a float32 NaN lane against s = 1.0 are:

| op | scalar overload (expected) | tensor overload | torch |
|---|---|---|---|
| gt, lt, eq | 0.0 | 0.0 | 0.0 (False) |
| **ge** | **1.0** | 0.0 | 0.0 |
| **le** | **1.0** | 0.0 | 0.0 |

giving `ge(NaN) = 1.0` while `gt(NaN) = 0.0` and `eq(NaN) = 0.0`, so within the scalar API alone, ge disagrees with (gt OR eq). A NaN *scalar* would make the entire output constant 1.0 for the same reason. I have not run this on hardware: the direction column is what the two artifacts above predict, and one run of the repro below confirms or flips it. The complement argument in the previous section does not depend on which way it lands.

### Same mechanism, second op: heaviside cannot emit NaN on any path

[`ckernel_sfpu_heaviside.h:28-31`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/main/tt_metal/hw/ckernels/wormhole_b0/metal/llk_api/llk_sfpu/ckernel_sfpu_heaviside.h#L28-L31):

```c
v_if(v < 0.0f) { v = 0.0f; }
v_elseif(v > 0.0f) { v = 1.0f; }
v_else { v = s; }
```

The output set is exactly {0.0, 1.0, value}; no path forwards the input. `torch.heaviside(NaN, v)` returns NaN. This finding is unconditional: whichever branch a NaN lane lands in (the v_else under unordered-false, the v > 0 branch if the compare is sign-bit based), the kernel manufactures a definite value from NaN, so `ttnn.heaviside(NaN, 5.0)` returns 5.0 or 1.0, never NaN.

### The fix already exists in the tree

`ckernel_sfpu_binary_comp.h` rejects NaN in every comparison family: eq/ne at [lines 62-63](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/main/tt_metal/hw/ckernels/wormhole_b0/metal/llk_api/llk_sfpu/ckernel_sfpu_binary_comp.h#L62-L63), lt/gt at [104-105](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/main/tt_metal/hw/ckernels/wormhole_b0/metal/llk_api/llk_sfpu/ckernel_sfpu_binary_comp.h#L104-L105), le/ge at [158-160](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/main/tt_metal/hw/ckernels/wormhole_b0/metal/llk_api/llk_sfpu/ckernel_sfpu_binary_comp.h#L158-L160), where the weak-ordered kernel stores 0 when `abs(a) + abs(b) > inf`. The `*z` unary kernels in `ckernel_sfpu_comp.h` carry the same chains. The tensor-scalar comparisons and heaviside are the only members of the family without it. This is the same 2023-unary versus 2026-binary split documented for fmod/remainder in #51441.

### Repro (needs hardware; float32, not bfloat16)

```python
import torch, ttnn
dev = ttnn.open_device(device_id=0)
x = torch.full((32, 32), float("nan"), dtype=torch.float32)
t = ttnn.from_torch(x, dtype=ttnn.float32, layout=ttnn.TILE_LAYOUT, device=dev)

ttnn.to_torch(ttnn.ge(t, 1.0))                  # scalar overload -> 2023 kernel; expected 1.0
ttnn.to_torch(ttnn.ge(t, ttnn.ones_like(t)))    # tensor overload -> 2026 kernel; expected 0.0
ttnn.to_torch(ttnn.gt(t, 1.0))                  # expected 0.0; ge != (gt or eq) if the row above is 1.0
ttnn.to_torch(ttnn.heaviside(t, 5.0))           # expected 5.0; torch gives NaN
torch.ge(x, 1.0)                                 # reference: all False
```

bfloat16 cannot carry the probe: host-side packing collapses NaN to +inf before the SFPU sees it ([`ckernel_sfpu_exp2.h:76-79`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/main/tt_metal/hw/ckernels/wormhole_b0/metal/llk_api/llk_sfpu/ckernel_sfpu_exp2.h#L76-L79)), and the tensor then legitimately compares as inf.

Refs #52036, #52930, #51557, #51441.
